name: The Olive Tree of Vouves
age_estimate: contested: at least 2,000 years, possibly up to 4,000

location.address: Ano Vouves, Kolymvari, Platanias municipality, Chania regional unit, Crete, Greece
location.neighbourhood: Ano Vouves village, next to the Olive Tree Museum of Vouves

access: Paid entry via the small Olive Tree Museum of Vouves next to the tree (historically a nominal fee, roughly 1-2 euro; some recent visitor reports say free, so state as approximate). Museum open daily April-October 10:00-19:00, November-March by appointment only. Publicly signposted, no permission needed.
transport: No public transport station nearby; reachable by car, roughly 25 minutes from Kolymvari and about 40 minutes from Chania city.
verify_notes: THE ANCHOR TREE, and its age is a genuine open scientific dispute, report both figures, do not resolve it. Tree-ring analysis (O. Rackham & J. Moody, 'The Making of the Cretan Landscape', 1996, cited in F.R. Riley, Oxford Journal of Archaeology 21(1), 2002) found the tree to be AT LEAST 2,000 years old. Separately, scientists from the University of Crete have estimated it at 4,000 years old (widely reported, e.g. Forbes 2025, Greek press 2025-2026), which would make it the oldest known living tree/olive in the world; this estimate is not tied to a single peer-reviewed paper in what I could fetch, it is consistently attributed to 'University of Crete scientists' across sources without a named study. English Wikipedia itself states plainly: 'The exact age of the tree cannot be determined,' and that 'there is not yet an agreed upon scientific method to ascertain the age of olive trees.' Reason the question is genuinely open: radiocarbon/radioisotope dating is impossible because the heartwood has rotted away and been lost over the centuries (this is normal for ancient olives, not a defect of this specimen), so any figure is an estimate from ring counts on remaining wood or comparative growth models, both of which carry wide error bars for a species that hollows out. A possible corroborating indicator: two Geometric-period (c. 900-700 BCE) cemeteries were found near the tree, which is suggestive but not proof of the tree's own age (do not bridge this into a claim about the tree, per the bridge-claim rule; Wikipedia itself only calls it 'a possible indicator'). Physical facts, not in dispute: trunk perimeter 12.5 m, diameter 4.6 m, hollow trunk (heartwood lost), still fruiting, grafted with the Tsounati cultivar. Declared a protected natural monument in 1997 by the Region of Crete. Branches were woven into olive wreaths for winners at the 2004 Athens and 2008 Beijing Olympics. Coordinate cross-checked: Wikipedia/geohack gives 35.48667N 23.78694E; an OSM natural=tree node named 'Elia Vouvon' sits at 35.4868591N 23.7868E, about 13m away, essentially the same spot beside the museum building (OSM way, tourism=museum, sits right next to it at 35.4870207/23.7867891). Used the OSM node as the tree-level pin. STORY ANGLE: lead with the age dispute itself as the fact, not a resolved number; it is more interesting than either single figure, and it is honest.

name: The Olive Tree of Azoria (Kavousi)
species: Olive (Olea europaea), local 'mouratoelia' variety grafted onto a wild olive rootstock

location.address: On the road from Kavousi toward Avgos, about 1 km south of Kavousi village, next to the Azoria archaeological site, Ierapetra municipality, Lasithi regional unit, Crete, Greece

access: Free, publicly signposted ('Old Olive Tree' / palia elia signs from the east entrance of Kavousi). Standing beside a public road and the Azoria archaeological site, no permission needed.
transport: No public transport; reachable by car, about 1 km south of Kavousi village, roughly 20 minutes from Ierapetra and about an hour from Agios Nikolaos.
verify_notes: Second major Cretan ancient olive, on the opposite (eastern, Lasithi) side of the island from Vouves. Official municipal source (ierapetra.gr, 'Memorial Olive of Azoria') states: tree-ring ('yearly ring') analysis dates its planting to between 1350 and 1100 BCE, i.e. roughly 3,100-3,400 years old depending on when measured. Widely-repeated press figure (Greek and international, e.g. GreekReporter Aug 2026) rounds this to 'about 3,250 years old.' Both figures come from the same underlying ring-count method and are consistent with each other, unlike Vouves; recorded as a range (3000-3400) rather than a single fabricated midpoint. Declared a natural monument ('Διατηρητέο Μνημείο της Φύσης') per EFSYN coverage of the official designation. Trunk: diameter 4.9 m, circumference 14.20 m. Notable as reportedly the oldest known example of olive grafting in the world: the visible tree is a 'mouratoelia' cultivar grafted onto a wild olive (agrielia) rootstock. Branches were used for the winner's wreath of the women's Olympic marathon at the 2004 Athens Games. GreekReporter's August 2026 piece (recent, dated this month) treats the tree as currently alive and fruiting, alongside the municipal page; both agree it still bears fruit today. Coordinates from cretanbeaches.com's stated GPS (35 06 54.78 N, 25 51 40.43 E, elevation 252m), converted to decimal; this is a named, signposted single tree beside a specific archaeological site so treated as confirmed precision despite not being an OSM-tagged node. STORY ANGLE: the grafting claim (oldest known graft in the world) is a good secondary hook alongside the age; note it is repeated across sources but I could not find the original scientific paper making that specific superlative claim, so treat per hard rule 8 (write it, say where it comes from, do not hedge in prose).

name: The Plane Tree of Krasi

location.address: Megali Vrisi square, Krasi, Hersonissos municipality, Heraklion regional unit, Crete, Greece
location.neighbourhood: the village square, beside the stone spring-fountain

access: Free. It stands in the open village square at Krasi, about 600 m above sea level, beside the stone fountain that still runs all year. Tavernas sit under the canopy, so the square is in daily use rather than fenced off.
transport: Krasi is roughly 12 km inland from Malia on the Heraklion coast, up the road towards the Lasithi plateau. A car is the realistic way; the village square is the centre of the village and cannot be missed.
verify_notes: GIRTH IS THE SOLID FACT AND THE AGE IS NOT. Two independent sources give the trunk perimeter as about 24 metres (cretanbeaches.com's monumental-trees series and exploringgreece.tv), which is the figure to publish, and it makes this one of the largest plane trees in Europe. It is described as an officially proclaimed Monument of Nature; the declaring instrument was not located this pass, so state the status as reported rather than as verified. AGE: DO NOT PUBLISH A NUMBER AS FACT. cretanbeaches.com states the age as 'estimated at 2400 years, as it is said that each meter of the perimeter represents 100 years of growth' - that is a local rule of thumb, not a published growth rate for the species, and it is arithmetic performed on the girth rather than evidence about the tree. Other sources round it to 'more than 2000'. So age_estimate is left EMPTY on purpose. AND THE REASON THE FIGURE IS SHAKY IS BOTANICAL, WHICH IS WORTH SAYING ON THE PAGE: oriental planes regenerate from the root, so a huge perimeter can describe a stool that has renewed itself many times rather than one continuously living stem. cretanbeaches.com makes exactly this point about the Gortyn plane (see crt_004): 'plane trees are constantly regenerating from their roots, seeming eternal, but actually being new trees.' Publish the girth, say nobody has dated it, and ask the reader. PIN: village-level from Nominatim (35.2343, 25.4672); no OSM natural=tree node was retrievable (Overpass returned 504 twice), so precision is approximate and the access line points at the square rather than a trunk. name: The Evergreen Plane of Gortyn

location.address: Gortyn archaeological site, Agioi Deka, Gortyna municipality, Heraklion regional unit, Crete, Greece
location.neighbourhood: at the back of the archaeological site, near the Odeon and the Law Code

access: The tree stands at the back of the Gortyn archaeological site, which charges admission and keeps daylight opening hours. Establish on the ground whether it can also be seen from the road outside; sources place it at the rear of the enclosure.
transport: Gortyn lies beside the old national road at Agioi Deka, about 45 km south of Heraklion in the Messara plain. A car or the Heraklion-Mires bus; the site entrance is on the main road.
verify_notes: WHAT MAKES THIS TREE WORTH A PAGE IS BOTANICAL, NOT MYTHOLOGICAL. It is an evergreen plane, Platanus orientalis var. cretica, a rare Cretan variety that keeps its leaves through winter while every ordinary oriental plane drops them. About fifty such trees are reported on the island. The Gortyn tree and the ones at Azogires in Chania are described as declared protected natural monuments. THE MYTH IS A FACT ABOUT THE PLACE, NOT ABOUT THIS TRUNK, and the two must not be joined. Gortyn is where Zeus, in bull form, is said to have brought Europa, and their union under a plane is depicted on the city's own ancient coins, which is genuinely good context. Nothing ties the individual tree standing there today to that story, and the page must not imply it. AGE: NOT ESTABLISHABLE, AND THE SOURCE SAYS WHY. cretanbeaches.com: 'plane trees are constantly regenerating from their roots, seeming eternal, but actually being new trees', and it notes this tree 'in its current form seems relatively small'. So the honest reading is a continuous rootstock rather than an ancient stem, and age_estimate stays EMPTY. Say this plainly on the page and ask the reader: it is more interesting than a number, and it is true. PIN: site-level from Nominatim (35.0590, 24.9513), approximate; the sources place the tree at the back of the enclosure but give no coordinate. No OSM natural=tree node found.
